answerWhyCheck.answer: Score 1/5 (Severe Security Failure). The response recommends raw SQL concatenation which introduces a critical SQL injection vulnerability regardless of firewall.

answerWhyCheck.answer: Score 2/5 (Factually Incorrect). Python's standard threading cannot execute CPU-bound work across multiple cores due to the Global Interpreter Lock (GIL).
answerWhyCheck.why: Reason 1: CPython's GIL restricts bytecode execution to one native thread at a time for CPU-bound tasks. Reason 2: True parallel core scaling requires multiprocessing, native extensions (C/Rust), or free-threaded Python.
answerWhyCheck.check: Benchmark CPU execution time across multiple threads vs multiprocessing using [Your Profiler/time.perf_counter] to measure core utilization.

answerWhyCheck.answer: Score 1/5 (Fundamental Accounting Calculation Error). Capital Expenditures (CapEx) is a cash outflow and must be subtracted, not added, in DCF modeling.
answerWhyCheck.why: Reason 1: CapEx represents reinvestment cash leaving the firm to acquire or maintain fixed assets. Reason 2: UFCF must begin with NOPAT (EBIT * (1 - t)), not unadjusted Net Income.
answerWhyCheck.check: Verify against standard financial modeling standards ([Your Source: Rosenbaum & Pearl / Wall Street Prep]) and reconcile cash flow from investing activities.

answerWhyCheck.answer: Score 2/5 (Dangerous Misunderstanding of Risk Limits). VaR provides a statistical confidence percentile, not a maximum ceiling or guarantee against tail risk.
answerWhyCheck.why: Reason 1: A 99% VaR explicitly implies that on 1% of trading intervals (2-3 days a year), losses will exceed the VaR estimate. Reason 2: VaR does not quantify the magnitude of tail losses beyond the cutoff.
answerWhyCheck.check: Execute historical stress testing and Expected Shortfall (CVaR) simulations using [Your Risk Engine: RiskMetrics/PyFolio].

answerWhyCheck.check: Apply False Discovery Rate (Benjamini-Hochberg) adjustment and test in a randomized controlled trial framework using [Your Statistical Library: R/statsmodels].
